subject: Post-demo: data territory & export-clearance checkpoints
messages:
From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@medicorehealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-04-18T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up from demo — compliance & residency checklist

Rachel — thanks for the walkthrough earlier today. Medicore's legal and security teams reviewed the session and compiled a short list of must-haves before we can proceed to procurement. Can you confirm the items below and share any relevant artifacts? We attached our standard vendor security questionnaire (Medicore_Vendor_Questionnaire.pdf).

1) SOC 2: do you have a current SOC 2 Type II? If so, can you provide the report or an attestation?
2) Data residency: we need confirmation that patient-derived PII/PHI can be served from an EU region (ideally Frankfurt) and not cross-border without explicit controls.
3) GDPR/HIPAA posture: high-level notes on processing agreements, DPA, and whether you support BAA for PHI workloads.
4) Export controls: any export eligibility or restrictions (OFAC/ITAR) we should be aware of for cross-border inference or backups.
5) Vendor questionnaire: please complete or return any sections you can and flag items needing escalation to your security team.

Timing: our procurement window aims for a decision by the end of May; security review must be complete before legal finalizes contract language.

Thanks — can you route to the right folks?

Best,
Sarah Li
Security Program Manager, Medicore Health
sarah.li@medicorehealth.com
Medicore Health

Attachment: Medicore_Vendor_Questionnaire.pdf (12 pages - answers requested)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@medicorehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — compliance & residency checklist

Sarah — great to connect today and thanks for the clear list. Quick replies inline below and next steps at the bottom. I've attached a copy of our latest attestation we can share immediately (Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025.pdf).

1) SOC 2: Redwood completed a SOC 2 Type II audit for our inference platform in Q4 2025. Attestation attached. For the full report we can coordinate an NDA/secure share — let me know the recipient for that.

2) Data residency: we have an EU region (Frankfurt - eu-central-1) available for hosted workloads and we support Dedicated/Private deployments inside a customer VPC for stronger isolation. By default, customer workloads pinned to EU do not leave the region; backups can be configured per policy. I will confirm backup residency policies with infra.

3) GDPR/BAA: We publish a DPA that covers GDPR controls; for HIPAA/PHI we support a BAA on enterprise plans. Marissa (cc) owns contracts and can start the BAA/DPA thread and share standard language.

4) Export controls: we have an export-eligibility process and an internal screening for OFAC/ITAR items. Short answer: common inference workloads are allowed, but certain controlled-data scenarios will require an eligibility check and may need mitigations (region-only deployment, restricted model variants). Karthik — see action items below for the matrix.

5) Questionnaire: we will begin filling Medicore_Vendor_Questionnaire.pdf; if there are place-holder items we'll return them with notes pointing to security contact.

Next steps (proposed):
- Karthik to provide a short export-eligibility matrix and technical notes (eta 24-48 hrs).
- Marissa to open contract/BBA/DPA thread and share templates (eta 2 business days).
- I will arrange secure share of full SOC 2 report if needed (please confirm recipient).

Timeline: we can target the security pack and questionnaire answers by 2026-04-20, then coordinate any follow-up with your security team the week after. Does that work on your side?

Rachel Kim
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com

QA notes and export eligibility matrix (high level):

Rachel / Marissa / Sarah — attaching a short export_eligibility_matrix.xlsx with rows for common data types and columns for: EU-hosted inference allowed, cross-border model artifacts, backup residency, and OFAC/ITAR flag. Summary below:

- EU-hosted inference (patient PII/PHI): Supported in eu-central-1. When pinned, inference traffic and persistent model state remain in-region.
- Backups: By default backups are region-local; cross-region replication is opt-in and can be disabled for Medicore.
- Model artifacts: Third-party model licensing may introduce export constraints; we will confirm model-specific restrictions for the licences you plan to use.
- OFAC/ITAR: Runtime itself does not export cryptographic functionality outside standard TLS flows, but customers processing embargoed entities or ITAR-flagged data will require an eligibility check. For those cases we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment and a contract clause restricting transfers.

Action items I will take now:
- Upload completed matrix to the secure share (JIRA-SEC-9876) and flag any models with special license restrictions (ETA 24 hours).
- Provide a short note on network egress controls and KV cache behavior for EU deployments (ETA 48 hours).
